We exist to wow our customers. We know we’re doing the right thing when we hear our customers say, “How did we ever live without Coupang?” Born out of an obsession to make shopping, eating, and living easier than ever, we’re collectively disrupting the multi-billion-dollar e-commerce industry from the ground up. We are one of the fastest-growing e-commerce companies that established an unparalleled reputation for being a dominant and reliable force in South Korean commerce.

We are proud to have the best of both worlds — a startup culture with the resources of a large global public company. This fuels us to continue our growth and launch new services at the speed we have been since our inception. We are all entrepreneurs surrounded by opportunities to drive new initiatives and innovations. At our core, we are bold and ambitious people that like to get our hands dirty and make a hands-on impact. At Coupang, you will see yourself, your colleagues, your team, and the company grow every day.

Our mission to build the future of commerce is real. We push the boundaries of what’s possible to solve problems and break traditional tradeoffs. Join Coupang now to create an epic experience in this always-on, high-tech, and hyper-connected world.

Role Overview

Coupang’s Cyber Threat Intelligence team is part of GHOST within Proactive Security under the Digital Trust organization. GHOST stands for Global Hunting, Oversight, and Strategic Triage. The organization proactively identifies and analyzes cyber threats that may affect Coupang and turns its findings into meaningful security actions.

The Cyber Threat Intelligence team collects and analyzes information from a wide range of sources, including open sources, commercial intelligence services, the dark web, and security telemetry. The team tracks threat actors and campaigns and identifies and responds to threats that may affect Coupang, including phishing, fraud, brand and executive impersonation, exposed data and credentials, malicious infrastructure, and high-risk vulnerabilities.

This position will primarily focus on intelligence activities that protect Coupang executives. You will continuously monitor digital exposure, impersonation, personal information exposure, phishing, social engineering, and other online threats affecting executives. You will turn analytical findings into actionable intelligence that supports timely protective measures and informed decision-making.

The focus of this position is intelligence-led executive protection rather than physical close protection. However, because information discovered in the digital environment may indicate potential risks to physical safety, you will work closely with Corporate Security, Legal, Privacy, Investigations, and other relevant teams.

Executive protection will be the primary focus of this position. Depending on team priorities and the candidate’s expertise, the role may also contribute to other Cyber Threat Intelligence responsibilities, including Fraud Intelligence, Digital Risk Protection, and third-party and supply chain threat intelligence.

This position is being hired at the Staff level and requires at least eight years of professional experience in a relevant security field. We are looking for someone who can independently lead significant and sensitive threat investigations, coordinate response and program improvements across organizations, and translate intelligence into executive decisions and meaningful protective actions.

What You Will Do

• Executive Digital Exposure Monitoring: Monitor executive-related digital exposure across authorized sources, including the open web, social media, professional networking platforms, data leak sites, the deep web, and the dark web. Distinguish legitimate online activity from potential risk and identify exposures that require further action.

• Executive Impersonation Detection and Response: Detect and analyze social media and professional networking profiles, email accounts, domains, websites, messages, images, audio, video, and other synthetic media that impersonate executives. Assess the intent and potential impact of the impersonation and coordinate blocking, notification, takedown, and follow-up actions with relevant teams.

• Personal Information and Credential Exposure Response: Monitor for external exposure of sensitive executive information, including contact details, addresses, account information, credentials, schedules, or location-related information. Assess the accuracy and risk of exposed information and work with relevant teams and external service providers to support removal, takedown, account protection, and other protective actions.

• Protective Intelligence and Threat Assessment: Investigate phishing, social engineering, Business Email Compromise, malicious disclosure of personal information, harassment, threatening references, and indicators of cyber or physical targeting involving executives. Assess source credibility, threat actor intent and capability, likelihood, and potential impact, and recommend an appropriate response or escalation level.

• Response Coordination and Case Management: When an executive-related threat is identified, promptly share intelligence and coordinate response activities with Corporate Security, Legal, Privacy, Investigations, Incident Response, and other relevant teams. Document investigative evidence and response actions and track progress and residual risk until the case is closed.

• Executive CTI Reporting: Provide executives and relevant leadership with clear and concise reports and briefings on their individual threat environment, significant cyber threats, impersonation and personal information exposure, and risks requiring immediate attention. Communicate complex threat information in a form that non-technical audiences can understand and act upon.

• Travel and Geopolitical Intelligence Support: As needed, analyze geopolitical conditions, civil unrest, crime, terrorism, cyber threats, and other security risks related to executive travel or major events and provide relevant teams with intelligence briefings.

• Support for Adjacent CTI Responsibilities: Based on team priorities and operational needs, support other Cyber Threat Intelligence activities such as Fraud Intelligence, Digital Risk Protection, third-party and supply chain threat intelligence, phishing and brand protection, and data exposure investigations.

• Tools, Automation, and AI: Use CTI and Executive Protection platforms, search tools, data analysis technologies, and AI-powered tools to improve the efficiency and accuracy of monitoring, classification, enrichment, investigation, and reporting. Validate AI-generated outputs against original sources and additional investigation.

• Global Collaboration: Work effectively with security teams, executive support organizations, engineering teams, business stakeholders, external CTI providers, and takedown service providers across the United States, Korea, and other regions to mitigate threats affecting executives and Coupang.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelors Degree in Computer Science or a related field
• 4 years of experience in Security Engineering or Cybersecurity

Preferred Qualifications

• At least eight years of professional experience in Cyber Threat Intelligence, Digital Risk Protection, Executive Protection, security monitoring, threat research, Fraud Intelligence, brand protection, incident response, security investigations, or another relevant security discipline
• Ability to lead or actively participate in meetings, prepare clear written reports and executive briefings, and clearly explain investigative findings and risk judgments to executives and global stakeholders
• Intermediate-level Korean proficiency, with the ability to communicate and collaborate with Korea-based colleagues in routine work conversations, written messages, and meetings
• Ability to investigate open sources, commercial intelligence, social media, the dark web, and other information sources and assess the credibility and limitations of collected information
• Basic understanding of digital threats such as impersonation, phishing, social engineering, personal information and credential exposure, account takeover, and online fraud
• Ability to assess the credibility, urgency, and potential impact of a threat based on incomplete or conflicting information and recommend an appropriate response or escalation path
• Ability to translate complex investigative findings into clear and concise reports that executives, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders can understand and act upon
• Ability to systematically manage time-sensitive threat cases and coordinate response activities involving multiple internal and external stakeholders
• Ability to handle personal information and sensitive investigative information with a high degree of confidentiality and discretion
• Ability to maintain professionalism, sound judgment, and composure when communicating directly with executives and senior leadership
• Professional-level Korean proficiency, with the ability to participate effectively in Korean-language meetings, prepare written business communications, and clearly explain security findings and judgments
• Experience in Executive Protection, Protective Intelligence, or Digital Risk Protection, including investigating executive impersonation, personal information exposure, phishing, malicious domains, and other online threats and pursuing takedowns or information removal
• Experience investigating open sources, social media, data leak sites, the deep web, and the dark web and operating commercial CTI, Digital Risk Protection, or Executive Protection platforms
• Experience assessing geopolitical and security risks affecting travel destinations, producing Travel Risk or Protective Intelligence reports, and collaborating with Corporate Security, Legal, Privacy, Investigations, or Crisis Management teams
• Experience in Fraud Intelligence, brand protection, third-party risk, or supply chain threat intelligence
• Experience leading significant and sensitive threat investigations or response efforts involving multiple countries and organizations and influencing executive and security leadership decisions and complex risk mitigation efforts
• Experience designing and advancing scalable Executive Protection, Digital Risk Protection, or CTI programs that define protected populations, monitoring scope, threat classifications, risk ratings, escalation criteria, and response procedures
• Experience developing long-term strategies for Executive Protection, Digital Risk Protection, CTI capabilities, or external intelligence partnerships and mentoring analysts or providing technical leadership

Pay & Benefits

Our compensation reflects the cost of living across several US geographic markets. At Coupang, your base pay is one part of your total compensation.

The base pay for this position ranges from $138,000/year to $297,000/year. Pay is based on several factors including market location and may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills and experience.

It is a senior individual contributor role for a product manager who can operate at the platform level while also working across real vehicle programs to ensure the full experience is coherent, intentional, and executable. You will report to the Director of Product Management and work closely with Design, Engineering, Program Management, and vehicle teams across GM. Define and evolve product requirements for core system UI capabilities, interaction patterns, and cross-surface experiences that span multiple displays and input modalities. Partner closely with platform PM, design, and engineering counterparts to ensure shared foundations are scalable, usable, and flexible enough to support multiple vehicle programs and brand expressions. Help drive clarity on what should be standardized at the platform level versus where intentional variation is required by vehicle, segment, or brand. Contribute to the long-term experience architecture for the digital cockpit, including how information, controls, system behaviors, and customer touchpoints work together across the vehicle. Vehicle Program Integration - Cohesive End-to-End Experience Represent the in-vehicle experience in partnership with vehicle programs to ensure the hardware and digital product come together cohesively. Work across vehicle programs and segments to translate shared platform capabilities into complete customer experiences that feel integrated across screens, controls, cabin architecture, and key moments of use. Ensure product decisions account for the full customer experience, not just what appears on screen — including the relationship between display layout, physical controls, cabin context, and driver or passenger expectations. C onnect platform strategy to a compelling vehicle experience. When data is incomplete, define learning plans through research, experiments, and instrumentation to improve decision quality over time. Experience operating across the full PM stack: product vision, roadmap, requirements, prioritization, decision-making, and delivery. Strong judgment in balancing near-term execution with long-term platform and product strategy. Platform & Multi-Surface Experience 4–6+ years working on platform-level or multi-surface products spanning multiple displays, form factors, device types, or interaction surfaces. Strong understanding of how system UI frameworks, interaction models, and design systems enable consistent experiences across diverse hardware. Comfort with hardware-software integration tradeoffs, including display constraints, rendering performance, input modalities such as touch, voice, and physical controls, and responsive or adaptive layout challenges. Experience helping define system behaviors, information architecture, content hierarchy, notifications, or shared UX patterns at scale. End-to-End Experience Integration Demonstrated ability to connect platform capabilities to complete customer experiences rather than optimizing only isolated features. Experience working across software, hardware, design, and delivery teams to bring integrated products to market . Ability to evaluate product decisions in context — considering the relationship between interface behavior, physical environment, customer expectations, and business intent. Track record of bringing clarity to ambiguous product spaces and aligning multiple stakeholders around a cohesive direction. Execution & Delivery 5–7+ years leading cross-functional delivery across engineering, design, program management, and operations in complex environments. Track record shipping multi-surface or multi-product experiences from concept through launch and post-launch iteration. Ability to navigate cross-team dependencies and drive alignment across platform , software, and product stakeholders. Skilled at resolving ambiguity through structured problem framing, crisp requirements, and clear tradeoff discussions. Customer Focus & Communication 4–6+ years leveraging customer research, market analysis, and competitive intelligence to inform product strategy and prioritization. Demonstrated ability to synthesize qualitative and quantitative insights into clear product direction and to establish measurement where it does not yet exist. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft clear, persuasive narratives for executive and cross-functional audiences. A hands-on, high-accountability mindset with a strong instinct to collaborate deeply and raise the bar for product quality and PM craft. Experience with premium or design-led products where quality, craft, and brand expression matter. jobs.description:
TL;DR
This is a senior hybrid role, half building the scaled programs engine, half account ownership. You'll own a cohort of scaled customers directly, running their onboarding, driving adoption, and retaining them, while designing the scaled enablement programs, curricula, webinars, onboarding journeys, and lifecycle communications, that teach an entire customer base how to build with Lovable.

Your book of accounts is a test bed and a live classroom. What you prove there becomes the playbook for the whole CS organization. This role suits a past CSM ready to multiply their impact through scaled education, content, and automation, owning revenue outcomes like a CSM while building like a program leader.

Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What you'll do

Scaled programs (~50%)

- Own post-purchase lifecycle communications and customer education across every channel and segment: email, in-app guides, Slack, release comms, and re-engagement plays

- Architect Lovable's customer education academy, defining learning paths, designing the curricula and content (courses, video, labs, certification-ready material), and owning the roadmap from first course to a full academy

- Build and host live education, including onboarding sessions, workshops, and feature deep-dives, turning recordings into an on-demand library

- Design the digital onboarding journey for scaled customers, with sequenced comms, in-app guidance, and self-serve resources anchored to the learning paths

- Package content into repeatable formats CSMs can deliver in their own accounts

- Instrument everything to tie education and program performance to retention

Customer ownership (~50%)

- Own a book of ~100s scaled-segment accounts end to end: run a disciplined renewal motion and manage risk early through direct engagement and automated plays, monitoring account health along the way, with most accounts self-served through your programs and your time reserved for moments of risk and opportunity

- Guide customers from first project to load-bearing app, helping admins deploy the platform well and helping builders ship applications their teams depend on

- Partner with Support to triage customer questions, keeping your time focused on proactive, high-leverage work

- Surface product blockers, expansion signals, and success stories to Product, Sales, and Marketing, capturing the voice of the customer

How we'll measure success
Scaled CS runs on the same core metrics as the rest of the team, no separate scoreboard.

- Gross retention (DRR/GRR) on your book, the north star for the segment

- Net active builders and net load-bearing apps, the impact of your programs across all accounts

- Education metrics: learning-path completion, live session engagement, and time-to-first-value for educated vs. non-educated cohorts

- Program metrics: onboarding completion, comms performance, and re-engagement conversion

- Leverage metrics: motions from your book that graduate to team-wide adoption

What we're looking for

- 6-8+ years in Scaled Success, customer success, customer education, or post-sales roles, with direct ownership of renewals and a track record of strong retention

- Deep experience designing and delivering one-to-many programs at scale: curricula, learning paths or academies, webinars, digital onboarding, lifecycle email, or community, spanning both instructor-led and self-serve formats

- A builder's instinct: comfortable prototyping with modern tools including Lovable itself, automating your own workflows, and using AI to extend your reach

- Strong written and presentation skills, sharp enough to write an email sequence that converts and hold a room of 200 customers

- Data fluency: you form hypotheses, instrument the programs to test them, and let results decide what scales

- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship, this segment is being built and you'll help define how it works

- Bonus: experience in a consumption/credit-based pricing model, PLG-to-enterprise motion, or developer/builder-adjacent products
